patch_description: Key change: replace the final bilateral one-pole damper (which adds lag and its own transient) with a fixed-λ Whittaker–Henderson polish using a second-order difference penalty. Evidence from the previous generation shows the one-pole damper's α ramp (0.60–0.95) leaks residual ripple and attenuates genuine dynamics — slope changes 15.2 and lag error 0.41 are the weak points. A constant λ = clip(25·(r_std/σ_r)², 1, 200), derived from the existing residual MAD statistics, applies a uniform penalty whose flatter passband suppresses residual ripple without the phase/lag cost of a stronger recursive filter. Solved with a banded (bandwidth-5) Cholesky in O(n) to keep runtime ~0.05s. Applied to the full-length signal and sliced last, preserving the `len(y) = n − window_size + 1` contract (a previous generation's zero score came from a length-changing post-smoother). The core robust adaptive Whittaker solve (Huber reweighting + curvature-relaxed local penalty) is retained since it drives the good tracking/responsiveness scores; only the post-polish is replaced.
